newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUNDESBANK HOLDS INTEREST RATES UNCHANGED.
newsitem.headline: BUNDESBANK HOLDS INTEREST RATES UNCHANGED.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.
The German discount rate, the floor on interest rates, remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate, the ceiling on interest rates, at 4.50 percent.
The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held unchanged at three percent.

Most economists had expecting the Bundesbank to leave interest rates unchanged at the meeting, although there is a growing view the central bank could lower the repo rate at a policy meeting sometime in the 1997 first or second quarter.

Support for a rate cut weakened after the Bundesbank said earlier on Thursday that growth in M3 money supply slowed only marginally in December, admitting also that its main monetary policy indicator had grown far beyond the 1996 target.
The German central bank said M3 grew at an annualised rate of 7.9 percent in December compared with its average level in the final quarter of 1995.
But M3 grew by 8.1 percent in the final quarter of 1996 from the final quarter of 1995.
The Bundesbank had set a four-to-seven percent growth rate for money supply between the fourth quarter of 1995 and the 1996 fourth quarter.
